searchDocs.title: What makes Strata easy?​
searchDocs.content: No session setup. Player sessions are handled automatically.No remotes to manage. Replication is built in.No separate type definitions. Your template provides types and autocomplete.No manual serialization. Supported Roblox and Luau datatypes are handled automatically.No manual saving. Data saves automatically, and you can still call Save when needed.  info For the best autocomplete experience, enable the new Luau type solver by setting Workspace.UseNewLuauTypeSolver to Enabled. Runtime functionality does not depend on it.

searchDocs.title: 1. Install Strata​
searchDocs.content: Install Strata via wally,  Strata = "soggybird0/strata-service@^1.1.0"   Or via model.  If the model is unavaiable, visit the latest github release and install the .rbxm file.  Place Strata inside ReplicatedStorage. Strata automatically creates its required runtime components and types.

searchDocs.title: 2. Create your data module​
searchDocs.content: Create a ModuleScript named Data inside ReplicatedStorage:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Strata = require(ReplicatedStorage.Strata) local Template = { Coins = 0, Stats = { Level = 1, Xp = 0, }, Inventory = {} :: { string }, -- `{ string }` Notifies Strata to use array types for this field } return Strata.Init({ StoreName = "Players", Template = Template, })   The template defines your data structure and provides the types used throughout your project.  New players receive the template, while existing player data is reconciled with newly added fields.

searchDocs.title: 3. Load and use data​
searchDocs.content: Server  local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Data = require(ReplicatedStorage.Data) Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(Player) local S = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player) if not S then return end S.Coins.Update(function(Coins) return Coins + 100 end) S.Inventory.AddNext("Wooden Sword") -- Adds to the end of the array (pos = #array + 1) end)   Client  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Data = require(ReplicatedStorage.Data) local C = Data.Client:LoadVault() if C then C.Coins.Observe(function(Coins) CoinLabel.Text = tostring(Coins) end) end   Every node has its own Observe. It calls your listener with the current value shortly after you connect, then again whenever that value changes. Use Changed instead if you only want the changes.

searchDocs.title: Working with data​
searchDocs.content: Strata provides methods based on the type of value you're working with.

searchDocs.title: Any value​
searchDocs.content: Get — Retrieve the current value.Set — Replace the current value.Update — Transform the current value.Observe — Receive the current value, then every change.Changed — A signal that fires on every change.

searchDocs.title: Tables​
searchDocs.content: Mutate — Modify a table.Snapshot — Retrieve a copy of the current data.

searchDocs.title: Arrays​
searchDocs.content: AddNext — Add an item to the end.RemoveLast — Remove the last item.InsertAt — Insert an item at a position.RemoveAt — Remove an item at a position.

searchDocs.title: Arrays and maps​
searchDocs.content: Has — Check whether a key or value exists.Keys — Retrieve keys.Values — Retrieve values.Size — Get the number of entries.Insert — Insert an entry.Remove — Remove an entry.Clear — Remove all entries.

searchDocs.title: Vault operations​
searchDocs.content: Save — Save the current data.End — End a session.Replicate — Request replication.GetSessionInfo — Retrieve session information.IsLoaded — Check whether a vault is loaded.  All data-node methods use dot syntax:  S.Coins.Get() S.Coins.Set(100) S.Coins.Update(function(Coins) return Coins + 1 end)   Observe works the same way on any node, from a single field to the whole vault:  S.Stats.Level.Observe(function(Level) print("Level:", Level) end)   Changed is the one exception to dot syntax. It's a signal, so it uses method syntax:  S.Stats.Level.Changed:Connect(function(New, Old) print(New, "was", Old) end)

searchDocs.title: Batched replication​
searchDocs.content: By default, Strata does not send a network message on every single write. Writes that happen in the same frame are queued, then flushed together at the end of the frame (task.defer).  What that means in practice:  Queue — Each Set / Update / Mutate / array write produces one or more patches and adds them to a per-session bucket.Defer — The first write in a frame schedules a flush. Later writes in that same frame only append to the bucket.Flush — At the end of the frame, the bucket is sent as one "Patch" replica (or one "Full" snapshot).

searchDocs.title: What Strata is for​
searchDocs.content: Strata is designed for player data.  It uses ProfileStore for session-based data saving and provides automatic client replication. It is not intended to replace systems such as OrderedDataStore or MessagingService for global data, leaderboards, or communication between servers.  The server owns all data changes. The client receives a read-only replica, and server-side changes are replicated automatically.

searchDocs.title: What's next?​
searchDocs.content: Working with dataConfiguration

searchDocs.title: BeforeMutate​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer.BeforeMutate: Signal<MutateContext<T>> Fires before every server write. Listeners can read the context but cannot cancel the write.

searchDocs.title: AfterMutate​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer.AfterMutate: Signal<MutateContext<T>> Fires after every server write.

searchDocs.title: OnSessionStart​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer.OnSessionStart: Signal<string,Player?, T> Fires after a session loads, before the client receives its data. Listeners get the save key, the player if there is one, and the data.

searchDocs.title: OnSessionEnd​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer.OnSessionEnd: Signal<string,Player? > Fires just before a session ends, with the save key and the player if there is one.

searchDocs.title: OnSave​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer.OnSave: Signal<string,Player? > Fires when Strata saves a session: a manual Save, or an AutoSaveSeconds save.

searchDocs.title: BindToMigrate​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer:BindToMigrate( Fn: MigrateFn<T>-- (data, fromVersion, toVersion) -> () ) → () Registers the schema migration callback. data is typed as your template. Requires SchemaVersion in Strata.Init config. Profiles whose saved version is lower run the callback once on load. local Data = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.Data).Server Data:BindToMigrate(function(data, fromVersion, toVersion) if fromVersion < 2 then data.Coins = data.Coins or 0 end end)

searchDocs.title: LoadVault​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> StrataServer:LoadVault( Target: string | Player ,-- A player, or a string key for data that is not tied to a player. Options: SessionOptions?-- Optional: Incognito (no save), Key override, KeyPrefix override. ) → State<T>?-- The vault, or nil if it could not load. Returns the vault for a player, waiting until their data is ready. Returns nil if the data could not load: the player left, or LoadTimeout ran out. Always check the result. local S = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player) if S then print(S.Coins.Get()) end local Guild = Data.Server:LoadVault("Guild_42") -- Never saves local Ghost = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player, { Incognito = true }) -- Saves under a fixed key local QA = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player, { Key = "QA_Profile_01" }) -- Load a key, but never write back local Preview = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player, { Incognito = true, Key = "Template_Starter", })

searchDocs.title: GetVault​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer:GetVault( Target: string | Player ,-- A player, or a string key for data that is not tied to a player. Options: SessionOptions?-- Optional key resolution (same as LoadVault). ) → State<T>?-- The vault, or nil if the session is not loaded. Returns the vault for a player if it is already loaded. Never waits.

searchDocs.title: IsLoaded​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer:IsLoaded( Target: string | Player -- A player, or a string key for data that is not tied to a player. ) → boolean Returns whether a session is loaded and active.

searchDocs.title: GetSessionInfo​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer:GetSessionInfo( Target: string | Player -- A player, or a string key for data that is not tied to a player. ) → SessionInfo?-- nil if the session is not active. Returns details about a session.

searchDocs.title: GetSettings​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer:GetSettings() → CachedSettings Returns every setting with its default applied.

searchDocs.title: GetPlayerFromKey​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer:GetPlayerFromKey( Key: string-- A save key. ) → Player? -- nil if no player owns it, or the key is not loaded. Returns the player who owns a save key.

searchDocs.title: ForEachSession​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> StrataServer:ForEachSession( Callback: ( Key: string, State: State<T>, Info: SessionInfo ) → ()-- Called once per session. ) → () Calls a function for every active session. Data.Server:ForEachSession(function(Key, S, Info) S.Coins.Update(function(Coins) return Coins + 5 end) end)

searchDocs.title: GetKeyFor​
searchDocs.content: Debug </> StrataServer:GetKeyFor(Player: Player ) → string Resolves the save key Strata will use for a player (respects PlayerKey, KeyPrefix, and Debug.Incognito).

searchDocs.title: ListKeys​
searchDocs.content: Debug </> StrataServer:ListKeys() → {string} Returns every session key currently loaded on this server.

searchDocs.title: OnReplica​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> StrataClient.OnReplica: Signal<T,ReplicaKind> Fires after every update from the server, with the new data and whether it arrived as a "Full" snapshot or a "Patch".

searchDocs.title: LoadVault​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> StrataClient:LoadVault() → State<T>?-- The vault, or nil if it could not load. Returns the local player's vault, waiting until the first replica arrives. Returns nil if nothing arrives before LoadTimeout runs out.

searchDocs.title: GetVault​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> StrataClient:GetVault() → State<T>?-- The vault, or nil if nothing has arrived yet. Returns the local player's vault if the data has already arrived. Never waits.

searchDocs.title: IsLoaded​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> StrataClient:IsLoaded() → boolean Returns whether the first replica has arrived.

searchDocs.title: GetSettings​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> StrataClient:GetSettings() → CachedSettings Returns every setting with its default applied.

searchDocs.title: RequestSync​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> StrataClient:RequestSync() → () Asks the server for a fresh full snapshot. Strata does this by itself when it notices a missed patch, so you rarely need it.

searchDocs.title: Storage​
searchDocs.content: Option	Default	What it doesStoreName	none	The DataStore name. Change it to start a fresh, separate store. Template	none	The shape and default values of a player's data. KeyPrefix	""	Prepended to the player's UserId to build their save key. PlayerKey	KeyPrefix .. UserId	A function (Player) -> string for full control over save keys. Mock	false	Uses ProfileStore's in-memory storage. Nothing is saved. Good for tests. AutoSaveSeconds	unset	Adds a save every N seconds on top of ProfileStore's own auto-saving.  Per-load key control (Key, KeyPrefix, Incognito) lives on LoadVault / GetVault, not in Init.

searchDocs.title: Sessions​
searchDocs.content: Option	Default	What it doesLoadTimeout	30	Seconds LoadVault waits before giving up and returning nil. KickOnFail	true	Kick a player whose data couldn't load, so they never play on empty data. KickOnSessionEnd	true	Kick a player if their session ends while they're still in the server. KickMessage	"Could not load your data. Please rejoin."	The message shown when a player is kicked.  caution Leave KickOnFail on unless you have a plan for players with no data. With it off, a player whose data failed to load stays in the game with no vault, and LoadVault returns nil for them.

searchDocs.title: Replication​
searchDocs.content: Option	Default	What it doesReplicateMode	"Hybrid"	How changes reach the client. See below. MaxPatchesBeforeFull	24	Once this many patches queue up in a frame, send a full snapshot instead. CollapsePatchesAt	12	If one Mutate changes this many keys in a table, send the table as a single patch. FlushImmediately	false	Send each change right away instead of batching them. ReplicateOnSave	false	Send a full snapshot to the client after every manual Save.  ReplicateMode takes three values:  "Hybrid" is the default. It sends small patches and switches to a full snapshot when a frame has too many of them."Diff" sends patches."Full" always sends the whole table. It's simpler to reason about, and it costs more bandwidth on large data.  Each replica carries a sequence number. If a patch is ever missed, the client notices and asks the server for a fresh snapshot by itself.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: Option	Default	What it doesClientGuard	"Proxy"	"Proxy" returns read-only tables from Get on the client. "Off" returns the raw table.

searchDocs.title: Leaderstats​
searchDocs.content: Name top-level fields that should appear on the Roblox leaderboard. They must be numbers, strings or booleans.  Strata.Init({ StoreName = "Players", Template = Template, Leaderstats = { Coins = true }, })   Strata creates the leaderstats folder and keeps it in sync with the data. You never touch the values yourself.

searchDocs.title: Private and transient fields​
searchDocs.content: By default, every field in your template is saved and sent to the client. Two options change that.  Strata.Init({ StoreName = "Players", Template = Template, Private = { Stats = { AntiCheat = true }, -- one field inside a table Secret = true, -- a root field }, Transient = { Combo = true, -- a root field only Cooldowns = true, }, })   Both mirror your template. Any key you leave out defaults to false, so it's saved and replicated as normal.  Private fields are never sent to the client. They're still saved, and everything on the server works as normal: Get, Set, Observe, signals. They can sit at any depth, and Stats = true hides a whole table. The client never receives them: not in the first snapshot, not in a patch.  Transient fields live in memory only and are never saved. Each session starts them from the template, so they're good for cooldowns, combos and anything that should reset when a player rejoins. They replicate to the client like any other field. They have to be root fields, because the saved data is stored as one profile.  Use both on one field to keep it on the server and out of the save.  note The client's types still list private fields, because the client and server share one template type. On the client those fields are nil.  Things to know:  Root Get, Set, Mutate and Snapshot include transient fields. Migrations only see saved data.A Private key that isn't in the template prints a warning. A Transient key that isn't in the template throws.Leaderstats works on transient fields.

searchDocs.title: Signals​
searchDocs.content: Strata exposes lifecycle and mutation events as signals, so you can connect from anywhere instead of passing callbacks into Init. A signal is a real object, so it uses method syntax (:Connect). Errors inside a listener are caught and warned, so a bad listener never breaks a write.  local Data = require(ReplicatedStorage.Data) Data.Server.OnSessionStart:Connect(function(Key, Player, SessionData) print("Loaded", Key) end) Data.Server.OnSessionEnd:Connect(function(Key, Player) print("Ended", Key) end) Data.Server.AfterMutate:Connect(function(Context) print(Context.Key, "changed", table.concat(Context.Path or {}, ".")) end)   Every signal also has Once and Wait.  Server  Signal	Listener receives	FiresOnSessionStart	Key, Player?, Data	After a session loads, before the client is sent its data. OnSessionEnd	Key, Player?	Just before a session ends. OnSave	Key, Player?	When Strata saves a session: a manual Save, or an AutoSaveSeconds save. BeforeMutate	Context	Before every server write. It can't cancel the write. AfterMutate	Context	After every server write.  Context has Key, Player, Data and Path.  Client  Signal	Listener receives	FiresOnReplica	Data, Kind	After every update from the server. Kind is "Full" or "Patch".  Data.Client.OnReplica:Connect(function(ReplicaData, Kind) print("Received a", Kind, "update") end)   Each node also has its own Changed signal. See Working with data.

searchDocs.title: Changing your template later​
searchDocs.content: Adding a field to the template is safe. Existing players get the new field and its default the next time they load, and any field whose type changed is reset to the template's value.  For changes that need real logic, like renaming a field or converting a format, set a SchemaVersion in Init and register a migration on the server with BindToMigrate. It runs once per profile, when that profile's saved version is older than yours.  -- Shared data module return Strata.Init({ StoreName = "Players", Template = Template, SchemaVersion = 2, }) -- Server script local Data = require(ReplicatedStorage.Data).Server Data:BindToMigrate(function(data, fromVersion, toVersion) -- data is fully typed as your template if fromVersion < 2 then data.Stats.Xp = data.Xp or 0 data.Xp = nil end end)   tip Bump SchemaVersion by one each time you ship a migration. The callback always receives the profile's old version, so you can handle players who skipped several updates in a single function. Call BindToMigrate once, early on the server (before or as players join). Without SchemaVersion in config, migrations never run.  caution Breaking (1.1.0): Migrate is no longer an Init option. Use Server:BindToMigrate so data stays typed.

searchDocs.title: Reading settings back​
searchDocs.content: local Settings = Data.Server:GetSettings() print(Settings.ReplicateMode, Settings.LoadTimeout)   The client has the same method, so shared code can check what it's running under.

searchDocs.title: Getting a vault​
searchDocs.content: There are two ways to retrieve a player's vault:  local S = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player) local S = Data.Server:GetVault(Player)   LoadVault waits until the player's data is ready. It returns nil if the data cannot be loaded, such as when the player leaves or LoadTimeout expires.  Always check its return value before using the vault:  local S = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player) if not S then return end   GetVault never waits. It returns the existing vault if the player's data is already loaded, otherwise nil. This is useful in code that runs after loading, such as remote handlers.

searchDocs.title: Non-player sessions​
searchDocs.content: You can also pass a string key instead of a Player:  local Guild = Data.Server:LoadVault("Guild_42")   This opens a session that isn't tied to a specific player. It can be useful for data shared across a guild, world, or other keyed entity.

searchDocs.title: Session options​
searchDocs.content: Both LoadVault and GetVault accept an optional second argument:  export type SessionOptions = { Incognito: boolean?, -- never save Key: string?, -- fully override the save key KeyPrefix: string?, -- override prefix for this load only }   Incognito (never saves)​  local Ghost = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player, { Incognito = true })   Incognito sessions use a unique throwaway key so the real player profile is never touched. Manual Save, autosave, and end-of-session saves are all skipped. When the session ends, local state is dropped without calling ProfileStore's end-save.  Key override (saves under a fixed key)​  local QA = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player, { Key = "QA_Profile_01" })   Behaves like a normal session, but stores under the key you provide instead of the player's default key.  KeyPrefix override​  local Prefixed = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player, { KeyPrefix = "Test_" }) -- key becomes "Test_<UserId>"   Incognito + Key (load a profile, never write back)​  local Preview = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player, { Incognito = true, Key = "Template_Starter", })   Loads that key's data into memory, then never persists changes. Useful for previews, spectating, or try-before-you-buy flows.  Option	Saves?	Key used(none)	Yes	PlayerKey / KeyPrefix .. UserId or string as-is Incognito = true	No	Unique incog_<guid> (or explicit Key) Key = "..."	Yes	Exactly that key Incognito + Key	No	Loads that key, never writes back KeyPrefix = "..."	Yes	Prefix + UserId (player) or Prefix + string

searchDocs.title: Reading data​
searchDocs.content: Every value in the template can be accessed through its corresponding node:  local Coins = S.Coins.Get() local Level = S.Stats.Level.Get() local Stats = S.Stats.Get()   You can access nested values by chaining keys. The returned value from Get corresponds to the node you called it on.

searchDocs.title: Client-side reads​
searchDocs.content: On the client, tables returned by Get are read-only proxies by default.  You can read and traverse them normally, but attempting to modify them throws an error. This helps prevent accidental local changes from making UI state disagree with the server.  If you need the raw table instead, you can disable this behavior with ClientGuard = "Off".

searchDocs.title: Writing data​
searchDocs.content: All writes go through node methods rather than direct assignment.

searchDocs.title: Set​
searchDocs.content: Set replaces a node's current value:  S.Coins.Set(50) S.Stats.Level.Set(2)   It also supports optional fields:  S.Equipped.Set("Wooden Sword") S.Equipped.Set(nil)   Both calls are valid because Equipped is optional in the template.

searchDocs.title: Update​
searchDocs.content: Update receives the current value and returns its replacement:  S.Coins.Update(function(Coins) return Coins + 10 end)   This is useful when the next value depends on the previous one.  Both Set and Update return the new value.  note Update always writes the returned value. There is no built-in "skip if unchanged" check. If you only want to write when the value differs, compare first: if S.Coins.Get() ~= target then S.Coins.Set(target) end

searchDocs.title: Type checks​
searchDocs.content: Writes are checked against the template. Setting a field to the wrong datatype errors instead of silently storing bad data:  S.Coins.Set("50") -- error: Strata: type mismatch at Coins — expected number, got string S.Name.Set(123) -- error: Strata: type mismatch at Name — expected string, got number   Rules:  Primitive leaves (number, string, boolean) must match typeof the template default.Non-empty tables in the template must receive a table.Empty {} collections (open arrays / maps) are not strictly checked.nil optional leaves are not strictly checked.  tip No direct assignment S.Coins = 50 -- throws Error: Strata: assign with .Set(value), not S.Key = value Data nodes aren't ordinary tables. Writes must go through their methods so Strata can track changes and replicate them correctly.

searchDocs.title: Mutating tables​
searchDocs.content: For changes involving multiple fields, use Mutate.  S.Stats.Mutate(function(Stats) Stats.Level += 1 Stats.Xp = 0 end)   Strata tracks the changes made during the mutation and replicates the resulting changes rather than requiring you to replace the entire table.

searchDocs.title: Snapshots​
searchDocs.content: Snapshot returns a deep copy of the current value.  local Before = S.Stats.Snapshot()   Unlike a read-only proxy, a snapshot can be modified freely without changing the actual vault.  This is useful when you need to keep a previous version of some data, prepare changes separately, or pass a copy to another system.

searchDocs.title: Arrays​
searchDocs.content: Strata provides methods for common array operations.  S.Inventory.AddNext("Wooden Sword") S.Inventory.AddNext("Shield")   AddNext adds an item to the end of the array and returns the new length.  S.Inventory.InsertAt(1, "Torch")   InsertAt inserts an item at the specified position, shifting subsequent elements.  local Removed = S.Inventory.RemoveAt(2) local Last = S.Inventory.RemoveLast()   RemoveAt removes and returns the item at a position. RemoveLast removes and returns the last item.  You can also use Size to retrieve the number of entries:  print(S.Inventory.Size())

searchDocs.title: Dictionaries​
searchDocs.content: Dictionaries use the same node API as other tables.  S.Items.Insert("sword_001", { Damage = 12, })   You can access individual entries directly:  local Damage = S.Items.sword_001.Damage.Get()   Use Has to check whether an entry exists:  print(S.Items.Has("sword_001"))   Remove deletes an entry and returns its previous value:  local Removed = S.Items.Remove("sword_001")   caution On array-like tables, numeric indices must use RemoveAt / RemoveLast, not Remove. Calling Remove with a number on an array throws so you don't leave gaps in the sequence.

searchDocs.title: Shared collection methods​
searchDocs.content: Arrays and dictionaries also support:  Keys — Returns the collection's keys.Values — Returns its values.Size — Returns the number of entries.Clear — Removes all entries.  These methods are available on both collection types.

searchDocs.title: Observing changes​
searchDocs.content: Every node has its own Observe, so you watch a field by walking down to it.  local Connection = S.Stats.Level.Observe(function(New, Old) print("Level is", New, "was", Old) end)   The listener runs once shortly after you connect, with the current value and nil as the old value. After that it runs whenever the value changes, with the new and old values.  The returned connection can be disconnected when you no longer need the observation:  Connection.Disconnect()

searchDocs.title: Choosing what to observe​
searchDocs.content: The node you call Observe on determines which part of the vault you're observing.  S.Coins.Observe(OnCoins) S.Stats.Observe(OnStats) S.Observe(OnEntireData)   S.Coins observes a single field.S.Stats observes the entire Stats table.S itself observes the entire vault.

searchDocs.title: Parent and child observations​
searchDocs.content: Observations account for changes throughout the selected node.  Observing a parent fires when one of its descendants changes.Observing a child fires when its parent is replaced.Unchanged values do not trigger another callback.  The listener's value is typed according to the node. For example, observing S.Coins gives the listener a number, while observing S.Stats gives it the corresponding table type. Your editor autocompletes the nodes as you walk down the template.

searchDocs.title: Changed​
searchDocs.content: Use Changed when you only want changes and not the current value. It's a signal, so it uses method syntax:  S.Coins.Changed:Connect(function(New, Old) print(New, "was", Old) end) S.Coins.Changed:Once(function(New) print("First change:", New) end) local New, Old = S.Coins.Changed:Wait()   Connect and Once return a connection you can disconnect, and Wait yields until the next change.

searchDocs.title: Client observations​
searchDocs.content: The client has the same Observe and Changed on every node:  local C = Data.Client:LoadVault() if C then C.Coins.Observe(function(Coins) CoinLabel.Text = tostring(Coins) end) end   There is no separate client observation API. Server-side changes are replicated, and client observations respond to those changes.

searchDocs.title: Sessions​
searchDocs.content: Strata manages session loading, saving, and cleanup automatically. You can still interact with a session directly when needed.  S.Save() S.End() print(S.IsLoaded())   Save requests an immediate save (no-op for Incognito sessions).End ends the session.IsLoaded checks whether the session is still active.

searchDocs.title: Session information​
searchDocs.content: Use GetSessionInfo to retrieve information about a session:  local Info = S.GetSessionInfo() print(Info.UserId) print(Info.LoadedAt) print(Info.LastSaveAt) print(Info.IsActive)

searchDocs.title: Iterating loaded sessions​
searchDocs.content: ForEachSession lets you perform an operation on every currently loaded session:  Data.Server:ForEachSession(function(Key, S, Info) S.Coins.Update(function(Coins) return Coins + 5 end) end)   When the server shuts down, active sessions are saved and ended automatically (Incognito sessions are dropped without saving).  To react to sessions starting, ending or saving, see Signals.

searchDocs.title: Metadata​
searchDocs.content: Each session has a metadata table alongside its data.  Metadata is stored with the profile, but it isn't part of the template. This makes it useful for bookkeeping values that don't belong in the main data structure.  S.SetMeta("LastDevice", "Mobile") print(S.GetMeta("LastDevice"))

searchDocs.title: Replication​
searchDocs.content: Server-side changes are replicated to the client automatically.  You don't need to create remotes, manually send updates, or request replication after every write.  Strata batches changes made within the same tick. This means multiple writes can be grouped into a single replication update instead of being sent individually.  The client receives a read-only replica. It can read and observe data, but all modifications must happen on the server.  To run code after every update the client receives, connect to Data.Client.OnReplica. See Signals.

searchDocs.title: Supported values​
searchDocs.content: Strata supports standard Luau values such as:  NumbersStringsBooleansOptional fieldsArraysDictionariesBuffers  It also automatically serializes supported Roblox datatypes, including Vector3, CFrame, Color3, UDim2, EnumItem, and DateTime.  These values are converted for storage and restored when loaded. You can use supported datatypes directly in your template without manually writing serialization logic.

searchDocs.title: Data limitations​
searchDocs.content: Strata follows ProfileStore's underlying data restrictions:  Arrays cannot contain gaps.Tables cannot mix numeric and string keys.Instances, functions, and threads cannot be saved.  Keep these restrictions in mind when designing your template.

searchDocs.title: Changed​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Changed: Signal A signal that fires when this node's value changes. Unlike State.Observe it does not fire for the current value on connect. It's a real object, so it uses method syntax. local Connection = S.Coins.Changed:Connect(function(New, Old) print(New, "was", Old) end) S.Coins.Changed:Once(function(New) end) local New, Old = S.Coins.Changed:Wait()

searchDocs.title: Get​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Get() → T-- The value at this node, or nil if there is none. Returns the current value at this node. On the client, tables are read-only proxies unless ClientGuard is "Off". local Coins = S.Coins.Get() local Stats = S.Stats.Get()

searchDocs.title: Snapshot​
searchDocs.content: Tables </> State.Snapshot() → T-- A copy of the value. Returns a deep copy of this node that you can keep or change without touching the real data.

searchDocs.title: Set​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Set( Value: T-- The new value. ) → T-- The new value. Replaces the value at this node. Throws on the client. Setting the root expects a table. S.Coins.Set(50)

searchDocs.title: Update​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Update( Updater: (Current: T) → T-- Receives the current value and returns the new one. ) → T-- The new value. Replaces the value at this node with the result of a function. Throws on the client. S.Coins.Update(function(Coins) return Coins + 10 end)

searchDocs.title: Mutate​
searchDocs.content: Tables </> State.Mutate( Mutator: (Target: T) → ()-- Receives the table to change in place. ) → () Changes several fields of a table at once. Strata works out what changed and replicates only that. Throws on the client. S.Stats.Mutate(function(Stats) Stats.Level += 1 Stats.Xp = 0 end)

searchDocs.title: Observe​
searchDocs.content: </> State.Observe( Listener: ( Value: T, Old: T? ) → ()-- Called with the new value and the old one. ) → Connection-- Call Disconnect on it to stop listening. Calls a function with this node's value now and every time it changes. The listener runs once shortly after you connect, with the current value and a nil old value, then on each change with the new and old values. Values that haven't changed don't fire again. Observing a parent fires when any child changes, and observing a child fires when its parent is replaced. Use State.Changed if you only want changes. local Connection = S.Stats.Level.Observe(function(Level, Old) print("Level is", Level) end) Connection.Disconnect()

searchDocs.title: Has​
searchDocs.content: Maps and arrays </> State.Has( Key: any-- The key to look for. ) → boolean Returns whether a key exists in this map or array.

searchDocs.title: Keys​
searchDocs.content: Maps and arrays </> State.Keys() → {any} Returns every key in this map or array.

searchDocs.title: Values​
searchDocs.content: Maps and arrays </> State.Values() → {any} Returns every value in this map or array.

searchDocs.title: Size​
searchDocs.content: Maps and arrays </> State.Size() → number Returns how many entries this map or array has.

searchDocs.title: Clear​
searchDocs.content: Maps and arrays </> State.Clear() → () Removes every entry from this map or array. Throws on the client.

searchDocs.title: Insert​
searchDocs.content: Maps and arrays </> State.Insert( Key: any,-- The key to set. Value: any-- The value to store. ) → () Sets one key in this map. Throws on the client. Arrays use State.InsertAt and State.AddNext instead. S.Items.Insert("sword_001", { Damage = 12 })

searchDocs.title: Remove​
searchDocs.content: Maps </> State.Remove( Key: string | any-- The map key to remove (not a numeric array index). ) → any-- The value that was removed, or nil if the key was missing. Removes one key from this map. Throws on the client. For arrays, pass a string key only if the array is being used as a map. Numeric indices on array-like tables must use State.RemoveAt or State.RemoveLast — removing by number would leave a gap in the sequence. S.Items.Remove("sword_001") -- map S.Inventory.RemoveAt(2) -- array S.Inventory.RemoveLast() -- array

searchDocs.title: AddNext​
searchDocs.content: Arrays </> State.AddNext( Value: any-- The value to add. ) → number-- The new length. Adds a value to the end of this array. Throws on the client.

searchDocs.title: RemoveLast​
searchDocs.content: Arrays </> State.RemoveLast() → any-- The removed value, or nil if the array is empty. Removes and returns the last value of this array. Throws on the client.

searchDocs.title: InsertAt​
searchDocs.content: Arrays </> State.InsertAt( Index: number,-- The position to insert at. Value: any-- The value to insert. ) → () Inserts a value into this array and shifts everything after it. Throws on the client.

searchDocs.title: RemoveAt​
searchDocs.content: Arrays </> State.RemoveAt( Index: number-- The position to remove. ) → any-- The removed value. Removes the value at a position in this array. Throws on the client.

searchDocs.title: IsLoaded​
searchDocs.content: Root only </> State.IsLoaded() → boolean Returns whether this session is still active.

searchDocs.title: Save​
searchDocs.content: Root only </> State.Save() → () Saves the session now instead of waiting for the next save. Does nothing on the client.

searchDocs.title: End​
searchDocs.content: Root only </> State.End() → () Ends the session. The player is kicked if KickOnSessionEnd is on. Does nothing on the client.

searchDocs.title: Replicate​
searchDocs.content: Root only </> State.Replicate( Target: Player? -- Who to send to. Defaults to the session owner. ) → () Sends a full snapshot to the client now. Does nothing on the client.

searchDocs.title: GetSessionInfo​
searchDocs.content: Root only </> State.GetSessionInfo() → SessionInfo?-- nil if the session is not active. Returns details about this session. local Info = S.GetSessionInfo() print(Info.UserId, Info.LoadedAt, Info.LastSaveAt)

searchDocs.title: GetMeta​
searchDocs.content: Root only </> State.GetMeta( MetaKey: string?-- The key to read. Omit it to get a copy of all metadata. ) → any Reads from the metadata stored beside your data. Metadata is saved with the profile but is not part of your template.

searchDocs.title: SetMeta​
searchDocs.content: Root only </> State.SetMeta( MetaKey: string,-- The key to write. Value: any-- The value to store. Must be JSON-compatible. ) → () Writes to the metadata stored beside your data.

searchDocs.title: GetPath​
searchDocs.content: Debug </> State.GetPath() → {any}-- A shallow copy of the path array. Empty at the root. Returns the path segments from the vault root to this node. Useful when writing generic helpers or logging which field changed. print(table.concat(S.Stats.Level.GetPath(), ".")) -- "Stats.Level"

searchDocs.title: GetKey​
searchDocs.content: Root only Debug </> State.GetKey() → string Returns the session key this node belongs to (e.g. "Player_123" or an incognito key when that mode is on).

searchDocs.title: DebugDump​
searchDocs.content: Debug </> State.DebugDump( Label: string?-- Optional prefix for the printed line. ) → () Pretty-prints this node's current value (or the whole vault at the root) to the output. Intended for Studio debugging. S.DebugDump() -- whole vault S.Stats.DebugDump() -- just Stats

searchDocs.title: Path​
searchDocs.content: </> type Path = {any} A path to a value as a list of keys. { "Stats", "Level" } points at Stats.Level.

searchDocs.title: Connection​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Connection { Disconnect: (...any) → ()-- Stops listening. Safe to call more than once. } Returned by Observe and by Changed:Connect.

searchDocs.title: Signal​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Signal { Connect: ( self: Signal, Listener: ( Value: any, Old: any? ) → () ) → Connection-- Calls the listener on every change. Once: ( self: Signal, Listener: ( Value: any, Old: any? ) → () ) → Connection-- Calls the listener on the next change only. Wait: (self: Signal) → ( any, any? )-- Yields until the next change, then returns the new and old values. GetId: (self: Signal) → number-- The raw Wire signal id, for advanced use. } The type of every node's Changed property. Typed per node, so the values match the field they come from. Unlike the rest of a vault, a signal uses method syntax: S.Coins.Changed:Connect(fn).

searchDocs.title: MutateContext​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MutateContext { Key: string-- The save key of the session being changed. Player: Player? -- The player who owns the session, if there is one. Data: T-- The session's data. Path: Path?-- The path being written to. } Passed to BeforeMutate and AfterMutate on StrataServer.

searchDocs.title: ReplicateMode​
searchDocs.content: </> type ReplicateMode = "Diff" | "Full" | "Hybrid" How changes reach the client. "Hybrid" (default) sends small patches and switches to a full snapshot when a frame queues too many of them. "Diff" sends patches. "Full" always sends the whole table.

searchDocs.title: ClientGuard​
searchDocs.content: </> type ClientGuard = "Proxy" | "Off" Whether tables returned by Get on the client are protected. "Proxy" (default) returns read-only tables that throw when written to. "Off" returns the raw table.

searchDocs.title: SessionInfo​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SessionInfo { Key: string-- The save key of the session. Player: Player? -- The player who owns the session, if there is one. UserId: number?-- The owner's UserId, if there is one. LoadedAt: number-- os.clock() when the session loaded. LastSaveAt: number?-- os.clock() of the last save, or nil if it hasn't saved yet. Seq: number-- Replication sequence number. IsActive: boolean-- Whether the session is still active. } Returned by State.GetSessionInfo and StrataServer:GetSessionInfo.

searchDocs.title: CachedSettings​
searchDocs.content: </> interface CachedSettings { StoreName: string-- The DataStore name. KeyPrefix: string-- Prepended to the UserId to build save keys. ReplicateMode: ReplicateMode-- How changes reach the client. MaxPatchesBeforeFull: number-- Patches per frame before a full snapshot is sent instead. CollapsePatchesAt: number-- Changed keys in one table before it is sent as a single patch. FlushImmediately: boolean-- Whether changes are sent right away instead of batched. ReplicateOnSave: boolean-- Whether a full snapshot is sent after each manual save. LoadTimeout: number-- Seconds LoadVault waits before giving up. AutoSaveSeconds: number?-- Extra save interval, if set. SchemaVersion: number?-- The current schema version, if set. ClientGuard: ClientGuard-- Whether client tables are read-only. KickOnFail: boolean-- Whether players are kicked when their data fails to load. KickOnSessionEnd: boolean-- Whether players are kicked when their session ends. KickMessage: string-- The message shown when a player is kicked. Mock: boolean-- Whether ProfileStore's in-memory mock is used. } Every setting with its default applied. Returned by GetSettings.

searchDocs.title: Signal​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Signal {} Generic Wire-backed signal. Parameterized by the values passed to listeners. -- Signal<string, Player?, T> Server.OnSessionStart:Connect(function(Key, Player, Data) end)

searchDocs.title: SessionOptions​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SessionOptions { Incognito: boolean?-- If true, the session never saves (manual, auto, or on end). Key: string?-- Fully override the save key for this load. KeyPrefix: string?-- Override the store KeyPrefix for this load only (applied before UserId / PlayerKey). } Per-load options for StrataServer.LoadVault / StrataServer.GetVault. -- Never saves Data.Server:LoadVault(Player, { Incognito = true }) -- Saves under a fixed key Data.Server:LoadVault(Player, { Key = "QA_Profile_01" }) -- Load a specific key, but never write back Data.Server:LoadVault(Player, { Incognito = true, Key = "Template_Starter" })

searchDocs.title: SharedStrata​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SharedStrata { Server: StrataServer<T>-- The server side. Only populated on the server. Client: StrataClient<T>-- The client side. Only populated on the client. } What Strata.Init returns.

searchDocs.title: Config​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Config { StoreName: string-- The DataStore name. Required. Template: T-- The shape and default values of a player's data. Required. Leaderstats: Flags<T>?-- Top-level number, string or boolean fields to show on the leaderboard. Private: PrivateFields<T>?-- Fields that are saved but never sent to the client, at any depth. Transient: TransientFields<T>?-- Root fields that live in memory only and are never saved. KeyPrefix: string?-- Prepended to the UserId to build save keys. Defaults to "". PlayerKey: ((Player ) → string)?-- Full control over save keys. Defaults to KeyPrefix .. UserId. Mock: boolean?-- Use ProfileStore's in-memory storage. Nothing is saved. Defaults to false. KickOnFail: boolean?-- Kick players whose data fails to load. Defaults to true. KickOnSessionEnd: boolean?-- Kick players when their session ends while they are in the server. Defaults to true. KickMessage: string?-- The message shown when a player is kicked. LoadTimeout: number?-- Seconds LoadVault waits before returning nil. Defaults to 30. SchemaVersion: number?-- The current schema version. Pair with StrataServer.BindToMigrate. AutoSaveSeconds: number?-- Extra save interval on top of ProfileStore's own auto-saving. ReplicateMode: ReplicateMode?-- How changes reach the client. Defaults to "Hybrid". MaxPatchesBeforeFull: number?-- Patches per frame before a full snapshot is sent instead. Defaults to 24. CollapsePatchesAt: number?-- Changed keys in one table before it is sent as a single patch. Defaults to 12. FlushImmediately: boolean?-- Send each change right away instead of batching. Defaults to false. ReplicateOnSave: boolean?-- Send a full snapshot after each manual save. Defaults to false. ClientGuard: ClientGuard?-- Whether client tables are read-only. Defaults to "Proxy". } The options passed to Strata.Init. Only StoreName and Template are required. Mutation and session hooks are signals on StrataServer, not options.

searchDocs.title: DebugConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface DebugConfig { dev: Studio -orientedhelpers.Allfieldsareoptionalanddefaultoff. Enabled: boolean?-- Master switch. When true, enables safer defaults for logging helpers. Incognito: boolean?-- Studio-only: every player load uses a unique throwaway key (does not save when paired with LoadVault Incognito; otherwise still writes under the throwaway key). Prefer per-load { Incognito = true }. IncognitoPrefix: string?-- Prefix for debug / per-load incognito keys. Default "incog_". LogWrites: boolean?-- Print every Set / Update / Mutate / array write with path and value. LogReplication: boolean?-- Print when full snapshots or patches are sent to clients. LogObservers: boolean?-- Print when a node's Observe/Changed signal fires. ForceIncognito: boolean?-- Allow Debug.Incognito outside Studio (use with care). }

searchDocs.title: MigrateFn<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> type MigrateFn<T> = ( data: T, fromVersion: number, toVersion: number ) → () Migration callback registered with StrataServer.BindToMigrate. data is your template type T.

searchDocs.title: PrivateFields<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> type PrivateFields<T> = {[string]: boolean | PrivateFields<T>} Fields that are never sent to the client. Mirrors your template at any depth: Secret = true hides a root field, Stats = { AntiCheat = true } hides one field inside a table, and Stats = true hides the whole table. Missing keys default to false.

searchDocs.title: TransientFields<T>​
searchDocs.content: </> type TransientFields<T> = {[string]: boolean} Root fields that live in memory only and are never saved. Each session starts them from the template. Missing keys default to false.

searchDocs.title: Version​
searchDocs.content: This item is read only and cannot be modified. Read Only </> Strata.Version: string The version of Strata.

searchDocs.title: Init​
searchDocs.content: </> Strata.Init( Options: Config<T>-- Your template and settings. Only StoreName and Template are required. ) → SharedStrata<T>-- The server and client sides of your store. Opens Strata for the current environment. Server is only populated on the server and Client only on the client. Each side uses its own field, so neither needs nil checks. local Data = Strata.Init({ StoreName = "Players", Template = { Coins = 0 }, }) local S = Data.Server:LoadVault(Player)
